main_text.l: Principia actionis, seu practica, sunt ex qui-
bus ratio morum, & actionum secundum vir-
Simplices; ut, bonum, honestum, justum, utile,

l.i: expetendum, fugiendum, malum, turpe.

main_text.l: Compositæ; ut justa sunt expetenda, injusta

l.i: fugienda, honesta amanda, turpia vitanda, virtus
est laudabilis, vitium est vituperandum, & hujusmodi
multa, quæ Syllogismorum practicorum prima λήμ-
ματα & materia sunt.
Hîc breviter ostendendum est, cur necesse sit fidem
primis istis principiis haberi, tametsi à priori sint
ἀναπόδεικτα. Prima namq; principia probari non
possunt.

main_text.l: Si-cut enim omnes homines non caci vident hunc solem,

l.i: & dum ipsum vident, necessario vident lucem: ita
omnes homines sani, naturae lumine, & Deus in
natura hominum accendit, vident honestū esse expetendu-
m, inhonestum fugiendum: quod qui negat, cum ratione
insanire censendus est, & stultior Anaxagorâ, qui nivẽ [?]
nigram esse contendit, contra omnium hominum co-
nsentientem & universalem experientiam. Sane qui
negat hæc principia, non est audiendus, juxta illud:
Contra negantem principia non est disputandum.

marginalia.note: Lumine naturae quod est mentibus humanis inditum.

page.notes: Greek ἀναπόδεικτα transcribed from a small, slightly blurred print; accents uncertain. The marginal note "Certitudo principiorum tribus modis cernitur." is set in a narrow column and is transcribed as one note. Last line is a hyphenated word continuing beyond this part. The first line is cut at the top of the scan, so "cut" is read as "ut" [?] and "caci" as "caeci" [?]; the initial word is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The "1." above the first note line is partly cut off. The quotation "Contra negantem principia non est disputandum." is set in roman type within the italic paragraph. "nivẽ" with a tilde over the e is uncertain. The "&" before "Deus" is an unusual glyph and is read as "&" with [?] omitted. The Greek letters are not present on this part.
